Actual Article Body:
Growing a bigger, cleaner energy grid.

How we make things matters.

Cleaner, cheaper and better transport choices.

Take Action

/

Climate Politics

Meanwhile, the rest of us are left footing the bill for the climate damage.

Higher insurance premiums, spiralling costs for imported fuel, and billions in disaster recovery from worsening fires, floods and heatwaves are among the costs we pay for fossil fuel pollution, and they hit harder every year.

But while everyday Australians tighten their belts, highly polluting coal, oil and gas corporations are raking in record profits and pocketing billions in government subsidies, leaving everyday Australians to pick up the tab for the climate damage.

It’s time for that to change. Right now, decisions are being made that will determine whether fossil fuel corporations keep getting a free ride at our expense, or whether they are held to account.

This is the moment to make our voices heard.

That means:

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - Tennessee was awarded $10.6 million through the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Fiscal Year 2026 to support strengthening statewide emergency warning systems.
